description: Compare Make, Zapier and n8n for business automation workflows, retries, monitoring, operational ownership and total cost. Integromat is an archived legacy name/platform for Make, not a fourth current competitor. Historical scores are provisional.

selectionCriteria.description: Use the same real business process and verify that every required app, trigger, write action, event payload and authentication flow is supported on the intended plan.
Simulate an API timeout, partial success and duplicate webhook delivery. Verify retries, backoff, alerts, idempotency, replay and who owns a failed workflow.
Test credential storage, least-privilege app connections, logs, personally identifiable data handling, retention, data region and user offboarding.
Model runs, operations, task steps, credits, retries, API quotas and spikes at expected workload. Verify the current billing model instead of assuming a flat price per user.
Measure the effort required to update field mappings, diagnose a broken integration, review version changes and restore critical flows after staff turnover.
Consider managed SaaS versus self-hosted deployment, server maintenance, data backup, upgrades, support commitments and the team responsible for recovery.

commonPitfalls: Treating Integromat and Make as two active competing vendors despite their documented rebrand and legacy shutdown.
Budgeting only on monthly users while ignoring task, credit, operation, run, API and retry-based billing.
Assuming a visual workflow is reliable without testing partial failure, duplicate events and recovery.
Using long-lived, overprivileged integrations without documenting credential owners or offboarding.
Launching dozens of automations without logs, alerts, version control or a maintenance owner.
Confusing successful trigger execution with a confirmed business outcome in the destination system.

faqs.question: Are Make and Integromat two different current automation services?
faqs.answer: No. Integromat was the earlier brand and legacy platform. Make announced the replacement, ended Integromat support on June 30, 2023 and shut down its platform on September 30, 2023. The historical record remains visible for context; compare Make with Zapier and n8n as current options. Official vendor source: https://www.make.com/end-of-integromat.

faqs.question: How should I choose among Make, Zapier and n8n?
faqs.answer: Start with a representative process across two or three apps. Test every required action, branching rule, retry, alert, permission and usage limit. Weigh the cost of runs or credits, hosting responsibilities, troubleshooting and maintenance; do not choose solely by an unsupported numerical ranking.

faqs.question: How much does business automation cost?
faqs.answer: Pricing depends on the vendor, plan, tasks, steps, operations or execution credits, hosting, API usage, support and how frequently failures require retries. Model real workload volume and compare the vendor's current billing rules. A universal per-user price range would be misleading.

faqs.question: What should I test before deploying an automation?
faqs.answer: Test success, timeout, duplicate input, missing field, revoked credentials and unexpected destination errors. Confirm how events can be retried without duplicate business records and who receives alerts. Keep records of the flow's owner, required access and recovery procedure.

body:
Best Automation Tools for Business 2026

Editorial scope: This is a use-case-based buying guide, not a paid ranking or a claim that one vendor wins for every team. Stored ratings and recommendations are decision aids; they are not a substitute for independently verified, current product evidence. Confirm capabilities, plan limits, data handling, and pricing directly with each vendor before purchase.

Business teams face unique challenges when selecting automation software. Budget constraints, scalability requirements, and specific workflow needs all factor into the decision. This guide evaluates the top automation platforms specifically for business use cases.

Shortlist to evaluate

Treat the following options as candidates to test against the same requirements. Product names, plan packaging, and capabilities can change; do not assume that a feature is included in every plan.

  • Make

    Teams comparing visual, multi-step workflows across business apps; test conditional routing, run limits, retries, and maintenance effort.

    • Test a representative multi-step process and its branching conditions
    • Check operation or execution limits and plan requirements
    • Validate logs, retries, alerts, and recovery from failed steps

    Verification step: confirm these capabilities, limits, integrations, and commercial terms in current vendor documentation and a representative pilot.

  • Zapier

    Teams prioritizing managed automation between commonly used SaaS applications; verify each required trigger and action.

    • Confirm each required app trigger/action and field mapping
    • Check task limits, branching, and paid-plan requirements
    • Test failure alerts, retries, and ownership of connected accounts

    Verification step: confirm these capabilities, limits, integrations, and commercial terms in current vendor documentation and a representative pilot.

  • n8n

    Teams that need control over workflow logic or deployment and can own the operational responsibilities.

    • Choose hosted or self-managed deployment based on team capacity
    • Test credentials, permissions, execution logs, updates, and backups
    • Model execution volume, maintenance, and recovery costs

    Verification step: confirm these capabilities, limits, integrations, and commercial terms in current vendor documentation and a representative pilot.

  • Integromat

    Legacy product name associated with Make; verify whether this record represents a distinct product or duplicate listing before scoring it separately.

    • Confirm the current product name and vendor identity
    • Do not treat a duplicate Make/Integromat listing as an independent competitor
    • Verify current plan terms before comparing scores or cost

    Verification step: confirm these capabilities, limits, integrations, and commercial terms in current vendor documentation and a representative pilot.

Selection criteria

Prioritize requirements before comparing feature lists. Mark mandatory requirements separately from preferences, and record the evidence used to make each decision.

  1. Affordability (Critical): Budget-friendly pricing for business teams
  2. Ease of Use (Critical): Quick onboarding for business team members
  3. Scalability (High): Ability to grow with business needs
  4. Integrations (High): Connect with existing business tools
  5. Support Quality (Medium): Responsive customer support for business teams

How to run a fair pilot

  1. Map one real process from trigger to final outcome, including exceptions and manual hand-offs.
  2. Test each required app connection, field mapping, branching condition, retry behavior, logging, and failure alert.
  3. Estimate execution volume and test what happens when limits are reached or an upstream service fails.
  4. Document who owns credentials, updates, monitoring, and recovery; include those responsibilities in total cost.
  5. Run a controlled pilot, reconcile outputs with the source systems, and only then expand to more workflows.

Common pitfalls

  • Choosing a platform that is too expensive for business budgets
  • Overlooking integration requirements with existing tools
  • Not testing the platform with real business workflows
  • Underestimating training and onboarding time

Calculate the full cost

Compare the subscription and renewal price, seats or users, usage limits, required add-ons, implementation and migration, training, integrations, ongoing administration, and the staff time needed to maintain the workflow. Use the same usage scenario for each candidate and ask vendors to confirm important limits in writing.

Decision checklist

  • Every must-have requirement has a documented test or current vendor source.
  • Unknown capabilities and plan limits are marked as unknown rather than assumed.
  • Data export, access control, failure handling, and exit steps have been reviewed.
  • The team has recorded trade-offs, recurring ownership, and the expected total cost.
  • The choice is based on the team's actual workflow rather than a universal ranking.

Revisit the decision when the team's workload, required integrations, operating constraints, or vendor terms change.

Legacy platform clarification: Make versus Integromat

Integromat is not a fourth independent current automation contender. Make's official history documents that support for the older Integromat platform ended in June 2023 and the platform was shut down in September 2023. The historical name remains here to help users understand older documentation and migration references, not as a viable new subscription recommendation. Official Make shutdown announcement.

Run one workflow end to end

Choose a representative process, such as moving a consented lead from a form to a CRM, notifying the owner, and confirming that the destination accepted the record. Test a duplicate event and an upstream timeout. For each candidate, record the exact trigger, action and authentication needed; measure how failures appear in logs and whether a replay creates duplicates. Calculate expected cost using normal runs, retries and likely growth rather than assuming every platform charges by seat.

Accountability and exit plan

Document workflow ownership, service account permissions, where secrets are stored, alert recipients, field mappings and data retention. Export or version the workflow configuration where supported. If operations require self-hosting, include backups, upgrades, incident response and credential rotation. A recommendation should be based on working evidence, not generic claims of easy setup or best-in-class performance.
